data.narrative:
Core Automation, a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, is targeting a Series funding round of $500M–$1B at a $4–5B+ valuation. The broader AI & Software sector contains 12 public and private comparables; however, the peer set for valuation triangulation is constrained by stage and valuation-tier specificity. One public comparable (Palantir, PLTR) and eight private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition are identifiable in the sector.

Peer-median analysis is not applicable here. Despite 12 same-sector comparables existing, the narrow filters required for methodological rigor—matching stage, adjacent-stage transition, and similar valuation tier—yielded fewer than three datapoints in any single cohort. A broad sector-level median would introduce uncontrolled heterogeneity and is therefore rejected in favor of disciplined non-application.

The stated target range of $4–5B+ reflects management expectations and investor appetite at the stealth stage, though independent validation through comparable company multiples is currently infeasible given data constraints. Key uncertainties center on market positioning relative to the identified peer universe, product-market validation metrics not provided in this dataset, and the degree to which stealth-stage positioning implies defensible differentiation or execution risk. Additional due diligence on revenue traction, customer concentration, and technical moats would be required to narrow this valuation range.
